summary.headline: Solara Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR 418 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR 77 crore, with PAT of INR 28.5 crore.
summary.overview: Management called Q2 FY27 its best quarter in about five years, with growth across revenue, gross margin, EBITDA and PAT despite West Asia-driven raw material and pricing pressures. The base business grew 37% YoY to INR 327 crore at a 23.6% EBITDA margin, while Ibuprofen came close to breakeven at a INR 91 crore revenue base. Net debt fell to about INR 500 crore from INR 614 crore at March 2026, helped by about INR 100 crore of rights issue proceeds, though it rose about INR 20 crore QoQ on working capital. The Ibuprofen strategic review has been extended by a further 12 weeks, with no decision yet.

segments.name: Base business (API)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 327 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA INR 77 crore at 23.6% margin; gross margin about 50%, below the 52-55% historical range due to mix and input costs. Regulated markets about 78% of revenue.

segments.name: Ibuprofen
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 91 crore (+21% YoY, +18% QoQ) on better prices and volumes; EBITDA loss narrowed to near breakeven from ~INR 9 crore loss in Q1 and ~21% loss margin two quarters earlier. Management calls the market commodity-like and the gain temporary.

segments.name: CRAMS
segments.commentary: Described as very small within the overall business; management is marketing services and chemistry to customers, with focus deferred to the core business.

guidance_outlook: Ibuprofen strategic review to conclude in about 12 weeks; options remain repurposing the plant into a multiproduct facility (including captive intermediates) or finding an external buyer.
Management is 'cautiously optimistic' and says a turnaround qualifies after two more quarters at or above Q2 levels.
Base business gross margin: management sees 52-55% as sustainable; adjusted for unrecovered raw material costs, reported ~50.5% would be ~53%+.
Cost base expected to stay flat, within plus or minus 2-3%, so incremental gross margin should flow to EBITDA.
Five DMF filings targeted for FY27: one in Q1, one in Q2, and three more by March 2027.
Capex commitment of INR 40-50 crore per year; net debt/EBITDA expected to stay in a similar range (~1.8x) over the medium term.
capex_capacity: Capex run-rate about INR 10-15 crore per quarter, within an annual commitment of INR 40-50 crore.
Vizag facility is mothballed with no current manufacturing; idle Ibuprofen-related equipment in CWIP sold for INR 4.5 crore.
Mangalore facility passed an ANVISA audit in August 2026; Cuddalore passed one in May 2026.
Debottlenecking and capex for high-margin products are planned to add capacity and lift EBITDA.
demand_pricing: Customers agreed to price increases; pass-through was about INR 25 crore in base business and INR 10-12 crore in Ibuprofen, so about INR 25-30 crore of the INR 418 crore revenue came from price and the rest from volume.

Base business gross margin was held back by raw material and solvent cost increases tied to the West Asia crisis; full pass-through is not achieved with every customer or product, and management expects this for one to two more quarters.
Ibuprofen demand rose this quarter; management says capacity additions in India and closures in the West may affect supply, and Ibuprofen is a commodity-pricing market.
KSM sourcing: about 60-70% India, 20-25% China, balance Europe. Container shipping delays pushed shipment lead times from 2-3 days to 5-7 days, lifting receivables at quarter end.
Strides (related party) contributed about 25% of business on average, rising to 30-35% in some quarters; INR 328 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vizag INR 4.5 crore exceptional item a one-off or the start of a wider reassessment of the INR 182 crore Vizag project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a one-off sale of idle Ibuprofen-related equipment in CWIP; no further Vizag charges are foreseen for now, pending the review.

qa_highlights.question: Trade receivables have risen more than fourfold YoY; what is driving this?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a ~50% rise in revenue, quarter-end billing concentration (last 7-10 days) and container shortages stretching billing-to-shipment from 2-3 days to 5-7 days; no payment terms were changed.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the net debt increase was from capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was about INR 10-15 crore per quarter; the rest was inventory build of about INR 20 crore to secure raw material.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin definition, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the accounting methodology is unchanged and it will take the input on board; base business GM is comfortable in the 52-55% range, and reported 50.5% would be ~53%+ after unrecovered raw material costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Ibuprofen business be profitable in the current quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot predict; Q2 breakeven depended on macro conditions and price increases, and it is hard to hold the same result in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vizag plant being sold, and are customers offering more volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Vizag is mothballed; management says it has not announced a sale and that strategic options cover CRAMS, Vizag and Ibuprofen, with a decision after the 12-week review.

risks_watch: Ibuprofen review outcome (sale or repurposing) due in about 12 weeks; management has already deferred the timeline once.
Receivables and working capital: trade receivables up more than fourfold YoY and rising inventory tie up cash; net debt rose QoQ.
Gross margin dependence on the West Asia crisis, solvent and raw material costs; Ibuprofen results may reverse if supply normalises, which the analyst asked about.
Related-party revenue from Strides (about 25%, up to 35% in some quarters).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the base business and financial recovery, but cautious and deflective on Ibuprofen, where management repeatedly declined to give timelines or outcomes beyond the 12-week review and framed Q2 gains as macro-driven.
key_quotes: Q2 FY 27 has been our best quarter in about five years.

Having said this, I will reiterate that the overall environment around Ibuprofen still remains challenging, and we haven't lost our focus on servicing large brands and marquee customers with whom traditionally we've had long-term associations.
We estimate that we will be able to close this in 12 weeks.
I'd be cautiously optimistic. I would say we've turned around if we can get another two quarters in line with the current quarter or better than the current quarter.

adds.what: Debottlenecking and capex for high-margin products (no specific capacity number given)

growth.why: Management guides a turnaround after two more quarters at or above Q2 levels and a 52-55% base gross margin, with growth backed by price pass-through (about INR 25-30 crore of the INR 418 crore revenue), customer volume gains and five DMF filings targeted for FY27, but no numeric revenue guidance or specific new capacity is given.
